notes: Status lines give the latest event I could verify on a fetched docket or primary page; the date in each status is the date of that event. Anything after it was not checked.

The web-search budget ran out mid-session. Topics from the brief I could not confirm and left out: H-1B $100,000 fee litigation (docket pages would not load), Southeast Asian refugee removal and TPS cases, public charge, hate-crime prosecutions of national significance, Section 203 language-assistance cases, census race-category cases, and Maui wildfire / Red Hill cases (no source tying them to AAPI or Native Hawaiian communities was found).

AANAPISI: I found no lawsuit specific to AANAPISI. The Education Department stopped operating AANAPISI and other minority-serving institution programs after a Dec. 2, 2025 DOJ Office of Legal Counsel opinion (OCA and CAPAC statements). The Hispanic-Serving Institutions suit (Tennessee v. Department of Education) is the related litigation.

Docket numbers I could not verify are marked in the dkt text. Cases flagged unverified: Jones Eagle v. Ward (docket numbers and any 2026 ruling not checked) and Mathis v. County of Siskiyou (court and docket not stated in the source).
For amicus entries, the x field gives the side stated on the brief cover where I read it. Positions are not otherwise characterized.

The AAPI link for DHS v. League of Women Voters, W.M.M. v. Trump, Genalo v. Black and Louisiana v. Callais rests on filings or statements by AAPI organizations, not on a case-specific finding about AAPI communities.

Source conflicts: ALC dates the Supreme Court's USPS stay denial Sept. 15, the Supreme Court docket says Sept. 14 (docket used). Press reports of the Fifth Circuit Wang v. Paxton ruling say both Wednesday and Thursday (Dec. 10 or 11, 2025). ALC's Dec. 23, 2025 release says the California CDL suit was filed that day; the court order says the petition was filed 12/29/25.

A summary of the ALC release on Trump v. Barbara said Justices Kavanaugh and Barrett joined the majority; the Supreme Court docket shows Kavanaugh concurring in the judgment and dissenting in part. The docket entry is used and is the place to read the vote.
OCA-Asian Pacific American Advocates v. Rubio: the Clearinghouse summary still says 'ongoing' but its docket entries show judgment on 2026-08-20; the docket entries are used.
